NOT GOOD, at first it seemed positive but the more I pressed on needing answers the more I was pushed away.  My rebuild took THREE separate rebuilds to get it right and the main reason was mistakes happen.  Bad management happens and happened!  The 2nd rebuild was passed off to me with a loose crank making an interesting nose but was told normal.  I said I'll take it home and drive for a bit and follow up, thinking maybe break-in noise?  well I did just that started up went for drive stopped let it rest (oil pressure at 10lbs.) tried to start it and wouldn't start.  Brand new battery and checked for condition and was 100% good....After a couple days I pin pointed noise myself to exactly what it was, but told by Todd it was probable manifold leak, accessory noice etc. etc. etc.  I eliminated all those possibilities but as doing so I did find several bolts loose, when told Toad he said it happens.  When I said not like this (something is big time wrong) he said I was now insulting him, WOW.  I also, took the pictures of the oil leaks, water leaks all over my garage floor, I had to take it right back, it was bad!!, could have ruined a numbers matching 1969 Mach 1 428CJ block but mistakes happen RIGHT?  Who am I to question the old mighty, I was providing vital information.  Did I mention the car wasn't even taken in there for a rebuild!!  It ran fine when I brought it there but found to have "YES" low oil pressure.  Lets rebuild, 1st rebuild less oil pressure, second you know the story and had low oil pressure.  Third, jury is out but (but good oil pressure and doesn't leak oil all over my new exhaust) if it needs a 4th I will not take it here even under warrantee.  It appears they kept some old parts off the car when they replaced them and claimed they gave them to me, lie!  Probably on ebay?  Joking hopefully not, but definitely not in my hands.
So frustrating to ask specific questions and never get the specific answer but just a lot of dishonesties.  I think they believe the customer is stupid, why else would the car be there right?  I ask to have proof of the engine components replaced and told they don't supply that, when I pressed him on that he send me a sheet for a totally different engine (same type but 3 years earlier and not my engine).  And a receipt of a cam left in the trunk, sounds like I got all the info....
I can't make this up, I could honestly write a book on all the misgivings/lies (white lies) I was presented, if I didn't know my cars and call him out who know what would have happened.
I do, 24k down the drain and and if messed up block make that another 24k.  MISTAKES HAPPEN though.

I had my 1961 T-Bird in for Carb work (tri-Carb) and subsequently had Front suspension work done there too  The primary Carburetor was working, but the other two were not- the linkage was not adjusted correctly. Since the parts were hard to come by, I supplied the parts, but several things were not installed- the upper and lower spring cushions, the front shock covers and the seat belts.
They seemed unfamiliar with the car, but proceeded anyway, the result is the carburetor is running too rich, the timing was not adjusted, which is a must when rebuilding a carburetor..
They claim to be restoration shop, but based on my extensive mechanical experience and background I found the work and followup  to be mediocre at best, plus it was expensive due to the lack of knowledge of the model car.

Every shop has it's challenges at times, I believe my 69 Mach 1 428CJ gave them plenty, my experience with them has been up and down.  24K in thorough engine rebuild with some rear-end and transmission stuff and seven months later still not right.  Todds engine builder/machine shop got fired for bad work to several engines and mine was one (no oil pressure).  After being pulled again, it was gone through by another and still have issues with noises/oil leaks etc.  When relaying this information or any information regarding quality of work I got mostly accused of being condescending, there's a pattern there.  I could go on, but you will most likely read it on his reply as you read in others with unpleasant experiences.
I really believe this is uncommon for this shop to hit the perfect storm which causes this unfavorable result but I can't bear witness to that.  I got car back 2 months ago and am trying to get it back in there to address pinging noise, there are other issues but have to choose my battles at this time in fear I wont get anything done? At this point I been told be patient and probably not drive and at two months still being patient.
I have faith Todd will step up and fix the issue but I have no evidence of that to write about.  Last after reading comments and speaking to Todd over the last year he does not take constructive criticism very well and while trying to be helpful he will tend to take that as an attack against  him or his mechanic Bob, when that is so far from the truth (Bob is really good).  So not sure how to read into that.  Actually I do but, I will hold that for now.  This isn't a positive or negative review just a factual experience.  No need for any attacks on them or me from them.
Will rewrite review accordingly to what the future holds.
Thanks for you reading, hope this helps....
I will have full details on my facebook page if you want a day by day experience.  I don't know if they are BBB accredited but can't find them so probably not.

I respect and love to support small businesses owners.  And I do believe Leo and his wife mean well.  However, as small business owners, you have to step up and stand by your work when things do not go as planned.
I used Highlife Audio Fabrication (HAF) to install speakers, amplifier and dashboard cam. Initially, I was satisfied with the installation Leo had done.  Unfortunately, on my drive home after the installation, I noticed that my airbag sensor was illuminated on my dash board.  I immediately contacted (HAF) to let them know.  Leo’s wife acknowledged the light and said that the sensor just needed to be reset.
First 🚩 When I return to have my airbag sensor reset, Leo informed me that my car might be part of an airbag sensor recall.  I explained to Leo that my airbag was not “on” when I brought my car to him and that I had just taken my car to the dealership for other recalls and that airbag sensors recall was not part of the recall list.  Second 🚩 🚩  We then waited for Leo’s friend to get off work with a sensor reader, so Leo could try to reset the airbag sensor.  Third 🚩 🚩 🚩 After not being able to reset the airbag sensor, Leo blamed the sensor on a “old” car battery.  I replaced the “old” battery with a new one and Leo was still not able to reset the airbag sensor.  Leo then had his wife explain to me that they were not going to be able fix the problem he caused and that I would be responsible to fix it on my own.
I gave Leo and his wife multiple opportunities to do the right thing.  They choose not to do so.  BUYER BE WARE.  You might have to take your car for additional repair work after you visit Highlife Audio Fabrication.

Very disappointed in this place, especially for being a place that specializes in auto upholstery. I brought in my BMW for door panel leather upholstery. They told me to pick leather to match and replace it, so I did. Took a couple weeks, then dropped off my car.

When I picked up my car, the job was so bad I was on the verge of crying. The edges were cut so short and lifted all the way around. The lifting was worse than how I dropped it off. I wished I had just not gone in there and kept my original leather. They claimed that the door panel was too difficult to get it tucked in properly, but had they seen the panel upon removing and seeing this as an issue, they should of refused to do the job, knowing they weren't capable of doing it.

The manager was nice and said he would get the job redone and fixed, so that is why I'm giving 2 stars, otherwise I'd give this place 1 star. The 2nd time fixing it was better than the first, although, I can't even say it looks decent. Still in my opinion not even acceptable. The sew job isn't even aligned straight on one door compared to the other. It is still lifting around the edges and they couldn't tuck it in, as they said before the door panel was tight. Smh, in the end, you get what you pay for. Redone twice and the pics are the end result after the 2nd time. You be the judge...They should be glad I'm not posting the first job pics, because I was shocked they thought picking it up that way was acceptable. I'm just shocked that this is an auto upholstery, but can't manage to do just that. Lesson learned, just dish out the money to get it done right at the dealership. I wasted a month of time just to end up having to get the job redone at the dealer.

I took my vehicle (Lexus) to a local auto dealership to have my seats replaced because the lumbar and several other electronic options within the seats were no longer working and the vehicle was still under warranty. The dealership told me that Lexus no longer manufactures those seats, so in order to have them fixed, the seats would have to be reupholstered. They stated that they would have to send my car to have the work completed to Trinity Auto Leather and Accessories, so I agreed and the vehicle was sent to their location in Garland. Upon receiving my vehicle back, I noticed that at some point during the repairs by Trinity Auto Leather and Accessories, they damaged/punctured several interior pieces of my car, including the center console and both the front driver’s side and front passenger’s side door panels/handle. When I informed the auto dealership about the damage to the interior of my vehicle, they reached out directly to Steve, the owner of Trinity Auto Leather and Accessories, who at first denied doing any damage at all to my car. Only after the dealership insisted that it be made right, Trinity Auto Leather and Accessories agreed to “fix the damage”.

Upon receiving my car again after the damage repairs, I saw that instead of replacing the pieces they had damaged, they simply packed the holes they had made with a putty-like substance that is a noticeably different color and texture from the surrounding surfaces of the undamaged areas. I am now stuck with a luxury vehicle that has several obvious flaws in the interior of the car due to no fault of my own; the damaged pieces should have been replaced and/or reupholstered instead of having putty packed into the torn areas/holes. Trinity Auto Leather and Accessories refuse to properly repair/replace the damage that they have caused to the interior of my vehicle. This is likely to affect the resale/trade-in value of my vehicle in the future, as the damage is still very noticeable.

I do not recommend this company to anyone, as they do not stand behind their work and they are careless when making repairs. Craftsmanship and integrity are very important factors to consider when choosing a company to take care of a luxury vehicle, and Trinity Auto Leather and Accessories is obviously devoid of both.
